stem.text:
Emily wants to save money to buy a car. She invests $dollar 180$ per month at an annual interest rate of $4.5 %$, compounded monthly. Determine, algebraically, the number of monthly investments she will need to make to obtain at least $dollar 15000$. Express the final answer as a whole number. Use the formula: $F V = frac(R ([ (1 + i)^(n)- 1 ]), i)$ where $F V =$ the future value

$& R = "the investment amount each period" \ & i = ([ frac("the annual interest rate (as a decimal)", "the number of compounding periods per year")]) \ & n = "the number of investments"$

extensions.latexSource:
Emily wants to save money to buy a car. She invests \(\$ 180\) per month at an annual interest rate

of \(4.5 \%\), compounded monthly.

Determine, algebraically, the number of monthly investments she will need to make to obtain at

least \(\$ 15000\). Express the final answer as a whole number.

Use the formula: \(F V=\frac{R\left[(1+i)^{n}-1\right]}{i}\)

where \(F V=\) the future value

\[
\begin{aligned}
& R=\text { the investment amount each period } \\
& i=\left[\frac{\text { the annual interest rate (as a decimal) }}{\text { the number of compounding periods per year }}\right] \\
& n=\text { the number of investments }
\end{aligned}
\]

solution.text:
$15000, = frac(180 ([ (1 + frac(0.045, 12))^(n)- 1 ]), frac(0.045, 12)), 1 / 2 "mark for substitution" \ 15000, = frac(180 ([ (1 + 0.00375)^(n)- 1 ]), 0.00375), \ 0.3125, = 1.00375 ^(n)- 1, \ 1.3125, = 1.00375 ^(n), 1 / 2 "mark for simplification" \ log (1.3125), = log (1.00375)^(n), 1 / 2 "mark for applying logarithms" \ log (1.3125), = n log (1.00375), 1 "mark for power law" \ n, = frac(log (1.3125), log (1.00375)), \ n, = 72.651539 ..., 1 / 2 "mark for evaluating quotient of logarithms"$

$therefore 73$ monthly investments are needed

extensions.latexSource:
\[
\begin{array}{rll}
15000 & =\frac{180\left[\left(1+\frac{0.045}{12}\right)^{n}-1\right]}{\frac{0.045}{12}} & 1 / 2 \text { mark for substitution } \\
15000 & =\frac{180\left[(1+0.00375)^{n}-1\right]}{0.00375} & \\
0.3125 & =1.00375^{n}-1 & \\
1.3125 & =1.00375^{n} & 1 / 2 \text { mark for simplification } \\
\log (1.3125) & =\log (1.00375)^{n} & 1 / 2 \text { mark for applying logarithms } \\
\log (1.3125) & =n \log (1.00375) & 1 \text { mark for power law } \\
n & =\frac{\log (1.3125)}{\log (1.00375)} & \\
n & =72.651539 \ldots & 1 / 2 \text { mark for evaluating quotient of logarithms }
\end{array}
\]

\(\therefore 73\) monthly investments are needed

extensions.latexSource:
Solve, algebraically.

\[
\log (x-1)+\log (x+2)=1
\]

solution.text:
$log [(x - 1)(x + 2)] & = 1 \ (x - 1)(x + 2) & = 10 ^(1) \ x ^(2)+ x - 2 & = 10 \ x ^(2)+ x - 12 & = 0 \ (x + 4)(x - 3) & = 0 \ x = - 4 x & = 3$

1 mark for product law

1 mark for exponential form

$frac(1, 2)$ mark for the permissible value of $x$ $frac(1, 2)$ mark for showing the rejection of the extraneous root

extensions.latexSource:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\log [(x-1)(x+2)] & =1 \\
(x-1)(x+2) & =10^{1} \\
x^{2}+x-2 & =10 \\
x^{2}+x-12 & =0 \\
(x+4)(x-3) & =0 \\
x=-4 \quad x & =3
\end{aligned}
\]

1 mark for product law

1 mark for exponential form

\(\frac{1}{2}\) mark for the permissible value of \(x\)

\(\frac{1}{2}\) mark for showing the rejection of the extraneous root

stem.text: Justify that there are only two negative terms in the expansion of $(- 2 x + 5 y)^(4)$.

extensions.latexSource: Justify that there are only two negative terms in the expansion of \((-2 x+5 y)^{4}\).

\(\mathrm{t}_{1}={ }_{4} C_{0}(-2 x)^{4}(5 y)^{0} \rightarrow+\)

\(\mathrm{t}_{2}={ }_{4} C_{1}(-2 x)^{3}(5 y)^{1} \rightarrow-\)

\(\mathrm{t}_{3}={ }_{4} C_{2}(-2 x)^{2}(5 y)^{2} \rightarrow+\)

\(\mathrm{t}_{4}={ }_{4} C_{3}(-2 x)^{1}(5 y)^{3} \rightarrow-\)

\(\mathrm{t}_{5}={ }_{4} C_{4}(-2 x)^{0}(5 y)^{4} \rightarrow+\)

The term is negative only when \((-2 x)\) has an odd exponent, which occurs twice.

1 mark
